data.long_meaning: Suchitra is a unisex name of Sanskrit origin meaning 'beautiful and well-crafted'. It has deep roots in Hindu mythology and culture. The name Suchitra carries the meaning “Beautiful and well-crafted” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Suchitra usually hope their child will grow to embody beautiful and well-crafted and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing divine beauty and skillful creation.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Suchitra total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Suchitra holds significant cultural value to Hindus. Suchitra is mentioned in the epic Hindu text, the Mahabharata, as the name of the contemporary of the great poet Kalidasa. The story goes that the king of Kashmir was so enchanted by the beauty of Suchitra, that he requested Kalidasa to compose a play for her, leading Kalidasa to write the famous play 'Shakuntala'. Thus, Suchitra carries the legacy of Indian art, literature, and culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Suchitra signifies the inner and outer beauty of a soul. It can be interpreted as a name given to a soul whose actions, thoughts, and intentions are beautiful and pleasing to the divine. Suchitra can also be seen as an encouragement towards leading a life of harmony and balance, thereby radiating inner peace and positive energy. The name can inspire individuals to strive for spiritual growth, where every action and every word bring pleasure to the self and the world around.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Suchitra means 'success in desired endeavors'. It signifies the attainment of one's heart's deepest desires through perseverance and determination. May the blessings of the gods grant you such success.

vedic_reference.note: Found in the Rigveda, a name for the goddess Saraswati.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu name Suchitra is derived from the Sanskrit word 'sukriti', which means good or virtuous deeds. It was a common name among Hindu females in ancient India.
historical_references.context: The use of such names was based on the belief in the importance of good deeds in attaining a virtuous life and ultimate salvation.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the name Suchitra can be found in the Indian epic 'Mahabharata'. In one of its chapters, the character of Subhadra, sister of Bhima and Arjuna, is referred to as 'Suchitra', which means 'a woman of good conduct'.
historical_references.context: The name Suchitra was also used to denote a woman of good character and morals, reflecting the societal values and cultural context of ancient India.
